subject: Follow-up: region affinity, hot vs cold backups, and cross-region failover
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Ava Clark <ava.clark@scouthealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 14:02:00 -0400
Subject: Recap + clarifying questions: region affinity, backups, and SR/DR assumptions

Hi Ava — thanks again for the productive call this morning. I wanted to capture the items we discussed and call out a few clarifying questions so our solutions and legal teams can align the proposal. High-level notes below (quick bullets), then proposed next steps at the bottom.

Quick recap of customer constraints we heard:
- Primary production traffic and PHI/PII stored must remain in US regions (customer-owned/RTO requirement).
- Cross-region failover allowed for DR, but failover must be explicitly invoked; automatic cross-border routing not permitted.
- Retention: transactional request logs retained for 90 days; conversational transcripts (user-facing) retained 180 days unless explicitly purged.
- Audit/logging: must provide immutable audit trail for access to logs and key management events.

Clarifying questions for your team:
1) When you say "US only" for model runtime, do you require both inference compute and persistent KV/store (chat transcripts, embeddings) to stay in the same US region, or is it acceptable to place ephemeral inference in a different US region (e.g., us-west1) while storing persistent data in us-east1?
2) For DR failover: what is the RTO target if the primary region is unavailable? Is a warm standby acceptable (minutes-level startup) or do you need active-active with sticky session migration?
3) Regarding backups: do backups need to be encrypted with customer-provided keys (BYOK) at rest? Any retention or retention encryption policy by regulatory team?

What we propose from Redwood for alignment:
- Region affinity: we can pin customer to a single US region for both compute and persistent stores by default; support for cross-region warm failover that is started by the customer and logged as a recovery event.
- Backups: nightly cold snapshots stored encrypted; option for BYOK for snapshots and S3-compatible exports. Cold backups can be geo-replicated within the US only.
- Logging/audit: redact PII at ingest for debug logs; full request/response audit trail stored in an immutable append-only store with access controls and time-based retention that you can configure.

Attachments included: region-affinity-matrix.pdf (draft mapping of pinning vs failover modes), redwood-residency-options-2027.xlsx (technical options + costs).

Proposed next steps:
- Ava: confirm answers to the 3 clarifying questions above and the RTO target.
- Scout Health Legal: share any minimum contract language about cross-border data movement or required audit artifacts.
- Redwood: we will prepare a short technical note (1–2 pages) mapping each option to cost & expected latencies and a draft failover runbook for your ops.

If that sounds right I can schedule 30 minutes next week to walk through the matrix and pick a preferred option.

Thanks — Jonas

Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 16:10:45 -0400
Subject: Re: Recap + clarifying questions: region affinity, backups, and SR/DR assumptions

Thanks Jonas — helpful summary. A few quick answers and a legal ask: 

Answers:
1) We require both inference compute and persistent storage to be within the US. Ephemeral inference in another US region is OK only if the persistent store (transcripts/embeddings) remains in the same pinned region.
2) RTO target: our ops team is aiming for <= 30 minutes for failover (warm standby acceptable). We are not expecting active-active.
3) Backups: must be encrypted with customer-provided keys. Our security team wants platform support for BYOK for snapshot exports.

Legal ask (cc'd): please confirm the minimum contract language Scout Health requires around explicit customer-triggered failover and an audit of each failover event (who initiated, when, what data moved).

Also: can you confirm whether Redwoods's immutable audit trail includes key rotation events from our KMS? That is important for our compliance reviewers.

Happy to do the matrix review next week — Tue or Wed morning PT works.

— Ava

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ava Clark <ava.clark@scouthealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 08:30:12 -0400
Subject: Re: Recap + clarifying questions: region affinity, backups, and SR/DR assumptions

Hi Ava — quick technical notes from our infra team to confirm feasibility and surface tradeoffs: 

1) Pinning model and storage to a single US region is straightforward; we support per-customer region pin configuration. Performance tradeoff: if inference compute is colocated with storage in the pinned region, latency to end-users on the west coast can increase ~10–40ms depending on model size; we will include measured numbers in the matrix.

2) Warm standby: we can maintain a warm standby in a secondary US region with pre-warmed images and cached model weights (cold KV). Typical warm startup to full readiness (including KV priming) is ~12–20 minutes for our standard LLM stack; heavy models (e.g., >60B) can take longer. We will include an option to pre-warm KV for prioritized endpoint paths.

3) Backups & BYOK: we support customer KMS (BYOK) for snapshot encryption and exports. Key rotation events from customer KMS are surfaced to our audit logs as distinct events. We also support HSM-backed customer keys for enterprise Private deployments.

4) Audit trail: immutable append-only store captures who initiated failover, timestamps, region IDs, and data-movement metadata. We will not store raw PII in debug logs; where required we can include hashed identifiers for correlation.

Action items from Redwood ops (we'll take ownership):
- Populate the attached matrix with measured latency numbers for the two candidate regions (us-east1, us-west1).
- Draft a short failover runbook that matches your <=30m RTO target (includes steps, permission gating, and rollback).
- Confirm KMS events and provide sample audit entries for legal review.

Jonas / Monica: I can run Tue 22 Jun 10:00 PT (13:00 ET) for the matrix review. Ava: confirm if that slot works.

Thanks — Marissa

Perfect — thanks for the quick responses, Ava. Confirming the plan and next steps so everyone has the timeline: 

Agreed scope:
- Region: US-only pin for both inference compute and persistent stores.
- DR: warm standby in a secondary US region, customer-triggered failover, target RTO <= 30 minutes.
- Backups: nightly cold snapshots with BYOK support; geo-replication within US only.
- Audit: immutable audit trail includes KMS key rotation events and failover initiation metadata.

Next steps and owners:
- Redwood (Marissa/Monica): update the region-affinity matrix with measured latencies and costs; draft failover runbook and provide sample audit entries for legal (due Tue 22 Jun EOD PT).
- Scout Health Legal: share minimum contract language and any non-negotiable clauses on failover by Tue 22 Jun EOD PT.
- Jonas: schedule 30-minute matrix review Tue 22 Jun 10:00 PT (tentative) — will send calendar invite once Ava confirms.

If there are any changes to the RTO or BYOK requirements please flag them now so we can include alternate options in the matrix.

Thanks — looking forward to the review.
